Ravenmarch (Ravenmarch, B48)

Region (English scoring-table region): Escann.

In brief: Bring the Corvurian exiled nobles' Raven Banner into Escann and establish a southern power supported by frontier knights, the Triumvirate Court, and a hidden vampire politics.

Narrative: High | Mission-tree length: Long (72 B48-specific mission definitions) | Mission-tree update: Based on local scripts supporting EU4 v1.37.5.0 | Distinctiveness: High | Waiting: Medium (formation, marsh management, and event chains) | Early pressure: High, depending on the adventurer start | Expansion capacity: High

Identity and Origins

Ravenmarch is not an independent kingdom already present in 1444. You begin as the Raven Banner (B14) adventurer band: the base game gives it Corvurian culture, the Regent Court faith, an adventurer reform, and a Corvurian ruler already in place in 1441. The current formation decision requires the Escanni adventurer state-building prerequisites, an Administrative Technology threshold, peace, and a foothold in Dostan's Way, Vernham, or Clovenwood; only then does it become B48 and receive its dedicated missions. [Local history script] [Local script]

The offline English Wiki's “Raven Banner” entry only establishes that it is a Corvurian-origin adventurer band led by Jherg of Corveld; the Ravenmarch page itself is almost only a country frame. More detailed family legends and the Dostanor restoration therefore mainly rely on current mission text and the period's official development diary, rather than filling an empty Wiki page with invented history. [Wiki source] [Local narrative text]

The Southern March's National Story

The opening missions begin on the roads, woodland, and marshes at the edge of southern Castanor: establish a defensive line, seize Veynham, and reconnect a region shattered by the Green Tide into a state. The official development diary traces the Raven Banner's motive to Corvurian nobles scattered after the Calamity of Daravan and presents restoring Dostanor as the campaign's aspiration. That is development-era background; in the current scripts, the territory, formation, and restoration remain a future the player must earn step by step. [Official development diary] [Local script]

After formation, the campaign does not only expand southward. The Triumvirate Court turns religion and court factions into institutional choices: unlocking its missions requires religious unity and theological preparation, after which decisions can adjust the balance among competing forces. The Marsh Restoration of Daravan's Folly turns conquered land into a long-term project rather than making it prosperous after a single war. [Local script]

The Court's Shadow and Later Expeditions

The base-game mission tree also introduces a vampire estate and associated privilege conversions. Masquerade and duel events among disguised nobles portray the march as a polity that venerates Corin while negotiating with powers of the night. Events can cost prestige and legitimacy, and extreme failures may even endanger the ruler; this is not merely a knightly country that paints the map. The exact political consequences of the vampires vary with the relevant missions and events, so the player nickname “soft vampire country” cannot establish a fixed conclusion. [Local script]

Later missions turn toward Dostanor, Divenhal, Bulwar, Salahad, and maritime trade routes. Older recommendation documents also list routes toward other great powers, but the current B48-specific tree does not directly prove that those names are inevitable continuous end-Tag transformations; only the confirmed expansion directions are stated here. [Local script] [Document record]

Personality and Recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 92/100 | Autocracy 78/100 | Magic↔Artifice 75/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; thematic intensity 65/100) | Pluralism 45/100.

The v2.1 value profile is Neutral (56/100) with a mixed trajectory. Rebuilding the march and managing the marshes provide public benefits, while vampire court politics and religious-unification routes carry risks of constraint and harm; conquest and monarchy are not treated as evidence of evil by themselves. Existing representative text is insufficient to label the entire campaign simply evil.

Recommended for players who enjoy Escann adventurer growth, southern frontier restoration, religious courts, and dark noble events. If you only want to form a strong country quickly and do not want court politics or long marsh construction, this campaign is more complicated than a simple knightly conquest.

Community Experience and Evidence Boundary

Official Development Diary 43 directly introduces the Raven Banner and Ravenmarch's story concept; two player posts discuss southern Castanor geography and comparison with Blade Marches gameplay, but neither supplies an exact version match to the current local files. [Official development diary] [Community opinion]

The offline Wiki's B48 page is an empty shell. Current formation conditions and special mechanics therefore follow the base Mod; detailed sources and gaps are listed on the evidence page.

National ideas (reference appendix)

Native English national-idea names and descriptions are reproduced below with the inherited effect displays. Traditions apply when this set is adopted; its seven ideas unlock with investment in idea groups, and ambition applies once all seven are unlocked. Racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. Alternative sets and successor ideas do not automatically stack. Descriptions may recount history or depict future ideals, not events already completed in 1444. Native English wording is reused rather than back-translating embellished Chinese localisation. Inherited display-unit assumptions remain unverified; this translation does not correct source data.

Ravenmarch (B48) — Ravenmarcher Ideas

Traditions: Ravenmarcher Traditions

Effects: Cavalry combat ability: +15%; global_manpower_modifier：+20%.

Idea 1: Shrouded Lands

Beyond Corvuria our people have settled, exiled from our lands drowned by Daravan's Folly, into lands obscured by the fires of villages burning by countless orcs. By establishing our strongholds in lands shrouded between hill and dale, our fortresses are both difficult to find and highly defensible. It will take an enemy far above the average skill to find our lands.

Effects: Fort defense: +20%.

Idea 2: Tested by Fey

On our voyage from Arca Corvur to Escann beyond, we encountered the ever-fabled Fey. As beautiful, and dangerous, as the legends say, we were tempted by the Fey to enter the Deepwoods proper and join them. Resolute in our mission, the Raven Banner ignored their charms, and set traps that night in case of retaliation. Later that night, that retaliation came, and Fey spirits attacked the camp. From then on the Raven Banner knew to always prepare for the enemy, and hurt them before they can ever harm you.

Effects: Hostile Attrition: +150%.

Idea 3: Vernham Heavy Brigade

The bravest and most noble of our soldiers swung great bludgeoning warhammers against the hordes of orcs. While they met great success in battle, reclaiming lands far from the heart of our new home, the age of heavy arms and armor soon came to an end with the ever-increasing use of firearms.

Veterans of these heavy infantry units assembled the Vernham Heavy Brigade, preserving their fighting style for future generations. However, their primary duty was to inspire courage and comradery amongst the greater army. Recruits were assigned to spar and wrestle with these great warriors. Although few could best them, all felt pride in themselves and gratitude for having the opportunity to improve their skills with these legends.

Effects: Discipline: +5%.

Idea 4: Sons of the Mire

The Raven Banner was established by Davan II síl Vivin of Corvuria in 1441 from the safety of Arca Corvur, to defeat the encroaching Greentide and claim lands for Corvuria. But in truth Jergan of Corveld, his fellow commanders, and their levied armies were exiles.

Frustrated by centuries of their lands ruined and drowned by the slow encroachment of Daravan's Folly, these nobles of the marshlands were a constant thorn to the monarch. Davan II saw an opportunity to be rid of this nuisance with the Greentide. The constant demands for supplies and funding to rebuild besoaked baronies, and intermittent rebellions from the lack of help, were too heavy a price to continue financing.

Jergan of Corveld, an eccentric but charismatic noble with dubious claims to the ruined city of Corveld, was summoned to Arca Corvur. Behind closed doors, the Raven Banner was established, outfitted with arms and supplies to drive deep into the Greentide. Eager to see them gone, and the deficit decrease, no binding agreements were made to ensure the loyalty of the Raven Banner to the holder of the Sapphire Key.

Effects: Army tradition: +0.5.

Idea 5: Reapers of the Bloody Harvest

All around us lie nations that threaten our way of life, ever on their mission to reclaim or pillage all of Escann. If they insist, the Ravenmarch will meet with fire and steel, and will stand victorious in the end.

Old Castanor has failed, crumbled, and burned into ashes. Once their lowly subject, Dostanor persists still despite the ruin of the Folly and bloodthirsty pretenders in Arca Corvur, but most of all in us. One day we will return, but for now Dostanor will be preserved in our hearths.

Effects: Army tradition from battles: +1.

Idea 6: Sisterhood of Ryala's Smile

Of all the gods of the Regent Court, Ryala of all has blessed our nation. Women and men both are fair, and true love is never heartbroken. The Sisterhood of Ryala's Smile upholds the tenets of Ryala in order to preserve our blessing, spreading the message of her smile even to beings such as orcs and goblins.

Ravenmarch was quickly swept up in the reformative spirit of the Corinite movement, remembering how they served with honor as the rear-guard of Corin's army. Their zealous hearts fixated on the role of Corin as a defender of the weak and a slayer of evil. But the old worship of Ryala and the death god Nerat did not wane in influence, and instead formed a triarchy of faith - life, war, and death.

Effects: Missionaries: +1; Female advisor chance: +25%.

Idea 7: The Lady with Dusken Hair

Legends say that in Ravenmarch, it is best to be wary of windows, for it is said that the Lady with Dusken Hair watches and listens through them. Former spies, hunched over in taverns far from any window, tell in horror how one by one their comrades were found lifelessly discarded in the streets, completely drained of blood. Even the commoners tell tales of how their seditious neighbours or family members would be found dead and drained, displayed prominently in the town square. They say that this Lady is an ancient vampire, and others go so far as to say that the government of the Ravenmarch has recruited these unholy abominations as spies.

Effects: global_spy_defence：+20%; Spy network construction: +20%.

Ambition: Ravenmarcher Ambition

Effects: Caravan power: +20%.

The current Mod gives the Raven Banner leader as Jergan of Corveld; the Wiki spells the name Captain Jherg of Corveld. The source difference is retained.
